item.title: Restricted and Undocumented oradebug Commands
item.description:
After an investigation into how to bypass restricted oradebug commands (see also 1), I started wondering whether a complete list of restricted commands exists, or whether there is any way to reliably identify them. Unfortunately, no such list is available, so I decided to take a closer look at the internal structures that oradebug uses under the hood.

To my surprise, I discovered that oradebug not only has restricted commands, but also a number of undocumented commands that are not shown in the oradebug help output.

item.title: Oracle Signal Handler Functions
item.description:
Signal handlers are programmer-defined functions that a process can register to respond to signals such as SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGSEGV.

When a signal is delivered, the operating system interrupts the normal execution flow and invokes the registered handler function, allowing the program to react and to clean up resources, log additional information, or terminate gracefully.

If no custom handler is registered, the system uses a default action, which in many cases means terminating the process or ignoring the signal.
